newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh reserves rise to 107.5 bln tenge.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh reserves rise to 107.5 bln tenge.

text.p: Kazakhstan's net reserves of hard currency and gold rose to 107.50 billion tenge ($1.42 billion) as of July 1 from 93.80 billion on June 1, the National Bank said on Tuesday.
It said the rise mainly reflected a rise in net currency reserves of 10.30 billion tenge equivalent, or 20 percent.
But gold reserves decreased by 3.30 billion tenge due to the fall of gold prices on international narkets.

Note -- July 1, 1996 data are provided in dollars only and July 1, 1997 figures are calculated on the basis of 75.50 tenge per dollar and a gold price of $334.05 per ounce. The bank gave no breakdown of currency and gold reserves for this year.
